entries.content:
**Account switching is feasible for both CLIs by selecting an account-specific directory when starting a new process.** The app does not currently do this: agent runs and usage polls inherit the same environment ([runner](/C:/Users/janbo/Documents/dev/md2/desktop/src/actions/agent/agent_runner_service.js:153)).

| CLI | Credential storage | Save and restore |
|---|---|---|
| **Codex** | `CODEX_HOME/auth.json` when file storage is selected; otherwise the OS credential store or process memory. | **Yes for file storage.** OpenAI explicitly documents copying `auth.json` to restore a login. Set a different `CODEX_HOME` per account. A keyring login cannot be assumed to be copyable. [OpenAI authentication docs](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth) |
| **Claude Code** | On Windows, `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\.credentials.json`, or `.credentials.json` under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`. | **Separate accounts are supported** by using a different `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` per account and logging in within each directory. Anthropic documents `/login` and `/logout` as managing the credential file; it does **not** document copying that file as a restore procedure, so that part needs a practical test. [Anthropic authentication docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication), [environment reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) |

Switching would need the selected environment applied consistently to runs, model discovery, and usage polling. Existing running CLI processes would retain their original account. Credentials are secrets, and expired or revoked logins may require signing in again.
